headline: WESDOME HITS 7.8 G/T AU OVER 57.2M AT KIENA DEEP — New Gold Zone Found Within 50m of Mine Infrastructure
snippet: Wesdome Gold Mines (TSX: WDO) confirmed the Norbenite Footwall Zone now traces over 150 metres vertically with hole N134-7207 returning 7.8 g/t Au uncapped over 57.2 metres at Kiena Deep near Val-d'Or, Quebec. Separately, six additional holes defined a new standalone VZ Zone discovered within 50 metres of existing mine infrastructure — a low-capital resource growth opportunity the company plans to define in a year-end resource update.

headline: GOLDMAN $4,900, JPMORGAN $4,500: What Wall Street's September Price Targets and Today's CPI Print Decide for Gold
snippet: With August CPI releasing this morning (September 11) and the Fed meeting September 15–16, GoldSilver maps every institutional year-end price target against current levels: Goldman Sachs at $4,900, JPMorgan at $4,500 for Q4, Bank of America at $4,360, and HSBC at $4,560. A cool core print holds rates steady and validates the bull case; a hot headline above 0.4% m/m lifts September hike odds past 70% and tests gold's floor near $4,350.

headline: HEMLO MINING DRILLS 89.9 G/T AU OVER 3.0M — 500-Metre South-Rim Zone Opens New Chapter at Ontario's Legendary Gold Camp
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. (TSX: HMMC) released additional assay results from its 2026 underground drill program at the historic Hemlo Gold Mine near Marathon, Ontario: hole 6702608 returned 89.89 g/t Au over 3.0 metres and 6702632 returned 14.81 g/t Au over 10.0 metres, both within the South-Rim Zone. The program has now traced approximately 500 metres of high-grade mineralization within the interpreted 1.5-kilometre zone, with roughly 1.0 kilometre of additional strike still to be drilled across a 130,000-metre total program.

headline: ARIZONA OXIDE GOLD STRIKE EXTENDED TO 1,250M+ — Aztec Minerals Hits 83.8m at 1.31 g/t AuEq at Tombstone, Maiden Resource Due Q4 2026
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT) extended the Contention mineralized system at its Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona by 255 metres to over 1,250 metres of continuously drilled oxide gold-silver strike. Highlight hole TR26-41 returned 83.8 metres grading 0.90 g/t Au and 22.61 g/t Ag (1.31 g/t AuEq), including 7.6 metres of 6.97 g/t Au and 75.42 g/t Ag. All five new drill holes hit oxide mineralization on ground largely undrilled by Aztec, with a maiden resource estimate targeted for Q4 2026.

headline: FIVE MARKET SIGNALS POINT THE SAME WAY Into the Fed's September 15–16 Rate Decision — And Gold Is in the Crossfire
snippet: GoldSilver identifies five independent signals all pointing toward a September Fed hike: options flow pricing 65% odds of a move, a Bloomberg Commodity Index surge to decade-plus highs, a sharp COMEX copper margin squeeze, HSBC's revised $108/barrel Brent call, and options market positioning in 90-day Treasuries. The analysis warns that inflation pressure is broadening well beyond gold's own headlines and heading straight into next week's FOMC.

headline: GOLD/SILVER RATIO'S 12-WEEK WHIPSAW: Swung from 61.7 to 70.4 and Back to 66.3 — What the Round Trip Costs the Unlucky Trader
snippet: GoldSilver's technical analysis tracks the gold-to-silver ratio's unusually wide 12-week swing — from a June low of 61.7 to a peak of 70.4 five weeks ago, back to 66.3 today — and argues the oscillation reveals how dramatically silver amplifies gold's rate-sensitivity. The piece provides a framework for sizing silver positions relative to the ratio's mean-reversion history, particularly relevant heading into a Fed meeting week.

headline: GOLD IS FALLING FOR THE WRONG REASON — Why Iran, Oil, and the Fed Create a Confusion Trade Most Investors Get Backwards
snippet: A counterintuitive analysis argues that gold falling during heightened US-Iran tensions isn't a safe-haven failure — it's an oil-shock transmission mechanism. Rising crude above $105/barrel feeds directly into CPI expectations, lifts Fed hike odds, raises real yields, and pressures gold: the safe-haven bid loses to the rate-hike math. Understanding this chain — geopolitical risk → oil → inflation → Fed → gold — is the key to not selling at the wrong inflection point.

headline: CAMECO'S PORT HOPE IS CANADA'S ONLY URANIUM REFINERY — A Strategic Bottleneck the Country Literally Cannot Afford to Lose
snippet: A Motley Fool deep-dive on Cameco Corp. (TSX: CCO) highlights the strategic chokehold of its Port Hope Conversion Facility and Blind River Refinery: these are the only commercial uranium conversion facilities in Canada, processing uranium ore into UF6 for enrichment into reactor fuel. With Cameco supplying fuel to 33 utilities across 33 long-term contracts and demand projections pointing to a doubling of global reactor capacity by 2040, replacing these facilities would take 10-15 years — making Cameco's infrastructure position as valuable as its mine production.

headline: USA RARE EARTH DOWN 60% FROM PEAK — After $2.8B Serra Verde Deal Closes and $1.55B Pentagon SPV Is Funded, Is It a Buy?
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) has fallen roughly 60% from its post-SPAC peak to $17.66 despite completing its $2.8 billion acquisition of Serra Verde — the only non-Asian producer capable of supplying all four magnetic rare earths at scale — and closing a $1.55 billion U.S. government-backed SPV with the Department of War committing $750 million. Q2 revenue of $5.82M missed consensus of $8.05M on heavy M&A costs, but management targets first magnet sales by year-end 2026 with 1,200-metric-ton Stillwater capacity planned for Q1 2027.

headline: DEBASEMENT TRADE ACCELERATES: China Dumps Treasuries to 2008 Lows, Netherlands Moves 86 Tonnes of Gold Out of North America
snippet: In the latest Money Metals Midweek Memo, host Mike Maharrey documents a cluster of central bank moves signalling accelerating dollar diversification: China reduced Treasury holdings to $652.3 billion — the lowest since September 2008; De Nederlandsche Bank moved approximately 86 metric tonnes of gold from North America to London between March and August 2026 citing rising geopolitical unrest; and U.S. interest expense reached $1.17 trillion through the first 10 months of fiscal 2026, up 15.5% year over year. Maharrey argues these data points reflect a slow-motion trust deficit in U.S. dollar and debt management.
